name: OLEFormat
description: Represents the OLE characteristics (other than linking) for an OLE object, ActiveX control, or field.
remarks: Use the OLEFormat property for a shape, inline shape, or field to return the OLEFormat object. The following example displays the class type for the first shape on the active document. Not all types of shapes, inline shapes, and fields have OLE capabilities. Use the Type property for the Shape and InlineShape objects to determine what category the specified shape or inline shape falls into. The Type property for a Field object returns the type of field. Use the Activate, Edit, Open, and DoVerb methods to automate an OLE object. Use the Object property to return an object that represents an ActiveX control or OLE object. With this object, you can use the properties and methods of the container application or the ActiveX control.

properties.name: Application
properties.description: Returns an Application object that represents the Microsoft Word application.

properties.name: Creator
properties.description: Returns a 32-bit integer that indicates the application in which the specified object was created. Read-only Long.

properties.name: Parent
properties.description: Returns an Object that represents the parent object of the specified OLEFormat object.

properties.name: ClassType
properties.description: Returns or sets the class type for the specified OLE object, picture, or field. Read/write String.

properties.name: DisplayAsIcon
properties.description: True if the specified object is displayed as an icon. Read/write Boolean.

properties.name: IconName
properties.description: Returns or sets the program file in which the icon for an OLE object is stored. Read/write String.

properties.name: IconPath
properties.description: Returns the path of the file in which the icon for an OLE object is stored. Read-only String.

properties.name: IconIndex
properties.description: Returns or sets the icon that is used when the DisplayAsIcon property is True. Read/write Long.

properties.name: IconLabel
properties.description: Returns or sets the text displayed below the icon for an OLE object. Read/write String.

properties.name: Label
properties.description: Returns a string that's used to identify the portion of the source file that's being linked. Read-only String.

properties.name: Object
properties.description: Returns an Object that represents the specified OLE object's top-level interface. .

properties.name: ProgID
properties.description: Returns the programmatic identifier (ProgID) for the specified OLE object. Read-only String.

properties.name: PreserveFormattingOnUpdate
properties.description: True preserves formatting done in Microsoft Word to a linked OLE object, such as a table linked to a Microsoft Excel spreadsheet. Read/write Boolean.

methods.name: Edit
methods.description: Opens the specified OLE object for editing in the application it was created in.

methods.name: DoVerb
methods.description: Requests that an OLE object perform one of its available verbs—the actions an OLE object takes to activate its contents.

parameters.name: VerbIndex
parameters.description: The verb that the OLE object should perform. If this argument is omitted, the default verb is sent. If the OLE object does not support the requested verb, an error will occur. Can be any WdOLEVerb constant.

methods.name: ConvertTo
methods.signature: ConvertTo([ClassType As Variant], [DisplayAsIcon As Variant], [IconFileName As Variant], [IconIndex As Variant], [IconLabel As Variant])
methods.description: Converts the specified OLE object from one class to another, making it possible for you to edit the object in a different server application or change how the object is displayed in the document.

parameters.name: ClassType
parameters.description: The name of the application used to activate the OLE object. You can see a list of the available applications in the Object type box on the Create New tab in the Object dialog box. You can find the ClassType string by inserting an object as an inline shape and then viewing the field codes. The class type of the object follows either the word "EMBED" or the word "LINK."

parameters.name: DisplayAsIcon
parameters.description: True to display the OLE object as an icon. The default value is False.

parameters.name: IconFileName
parameters.description: The file that contains the icon to be displayed.

parameters.name: IconIndex
parameters.description: The index number of the icon within IconFileName. The order of icons in the specified file corresponds to the order in which the icons appear in the Change Icon dialog box (Insert Object dialog box) when the Display as icon check box is selected. The first icon in the file has the index number 0 (zero). If an icon with the given index number doesn't exist in IconFileName, the icon with the index number 1 (the second icon in the file) is used. The default value is 0 (zero).

parameters.name: IconLabel
parameters.description: A label (caption) to be displayed beneath the icon.

methods.name: ActivateAs
methods.description: Sets the Windows registry value that determines the default application used to activate the specified OLE object.

parameters.name: ClassType
parameters.description: The name of the application in which an OLE object is opened. To see a list of object types that the OLE object can be activated as, click the object and then open the Convert dialog box. You can find the ClassType string by inserting an object as an inline shape and then viewing the field codes. The class type of the object follows either the word "EMBED" or the word "LINK."
